```{r}
# ============================================================
# Per-individual diagnostic plots used to verify M- and E-peak
# calls by eye (one PDF page per channel).
#
# PREREQUISITE: run Fig3_FigS2_activity_peaks.Rmd first, in the
# same R session. This script reuses its settings (input files,
# exclusions, lights-on/off times, DD_DAYS, loess_span, ma_k,
# half_window_h) and functions (get_va_curves(), find_va_peaks(),
# select_va_peak_in_window(), ch_to_abscol()).
#
# Output: review_Cxpip_SD.pdf, review_Cxquin_SD.pdf,
#         review_Cxpip_LD.pdf, review_Cxquin_LD.pdf
# ============================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(zoo)

# ---- Rebuild the per-channel averaged (raw, unsmoothed) DD profile
# for every channel in one file at once (same logic as
# extract_phase_offsets(), factored out here for reuse across all
# channels in a single pass rather than one file-read per channel). ----
build_all_channel_profiles <- function(file_path, exclude_ch) {
  raw <- readr::read_tsv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  exclude_abs <- ch_to_abscol(exclude_ch)
  keep_abs    <- setdiff(activity_start_col:activity_end_col, exclude_abs)

  act <- raw %>%
    select(all_of(names(raw)[keep_abs])) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))

  n_min      <- nrow(act)
  total_days <- ceiling(n_min / 1440)
  dd_start   <- total_days - DD_DAYS + 1
  dd_end     <- total_days

  long_full <- act %>%
    mutate(t_min = row_number() - 1, day = floor(t_min / 1440) + 1, tod = (t_min %% 1440) / 60) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(t_min, day, tod), names_to = "colname", values_to = "activity") %>%
    mutate(abscol = match(colname, names(raw)), channel = abscol - activity_start_col + 1)

  dd_raw <- long_full %>% filter(day >= dd_start, day <= dd_end)

  dd_raw %>%
    group_by(channel, tod) %>%
    summarise(activity_mean = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(channel, tod)
}

# ---- Build one diagnostic ggplot for a single individual. Shows the
# raw activity trace (grey bars) against the moving-average curve
# (navy) -- these are the two curves actually intersected by
# find_va_peaks() per Vaze et al. The loess curve (dotted grey) is
# shown only as smoothing context, since it feeds the moving-average
# curve but is not itself one of the two intersected curves. ----
plot_channel_diagnostic <- function(tod, activity, LON, LOFF, halfwidth,
                                     channel_label, span = loess_span, k = ma_k) {
  curve <- get_va_curves(tod, activity, span, k) %>%
    filter(t >= 24, t < 48) %>%
    mutate(tod = t - 24)

  va_peaks <- find_va_peaks(tod, activity, span, k)
  M_sel <- select_va_peak_in_window(va_peaks, LON,  halfwidth)
  E_sel <- select_va_peak_in_window(va_peaks, LOFF, halfwidth)

  sel_points <- bind_rows(
    if (!is.na(M_sel$tod)) tibble(tod = M_sel$tod, y = M_sel$y_cross, label = "M") else NULL,
    if (!is.na(E_sel$tod)) tibble(tod = E_sel$tod, y = E_sel$y_cross, label = "E") else NULL
  )
  if (nrow(sel_points) == 0) sel_points <- tibble(tod = numeric(0), y = numeric(0), label = character(0))

  other_peaks <- if (nrow(va_peaks) > 0 && nrow(sel_points) > 0) {
    va_peaks %>% filter(!(tod %in% sel_points$tod))
  } else {
    va_peaks
  }

  raw_df <- tibble(tod = tod, activity = activity)

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_col(data = raw_df, aes(x = tod, y = activity), fill = "grey70", width = 1/60) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = LON - halfwidth, xmax = LON + halfwidth,
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08, fill = "orange") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = LOFF - halfwidth, xmax = LOFF + halfwidth,
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08, fill = "blue") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = LON,  linetype = "dashed", color = "orange3") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = LOFF, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue3") +
    # Loess curve: shown as context (thin, muted) -- it feeds the
    # moving-average curve below but is NOT itself one of the two
    # curves being intersected.
    geom_line(data = curve, aes(x = tod, y = loess_y), color = "grey40",
              linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    # Moving-average curve: THIS is the curve intersected against the
    # raw activity bars above, per Vaze et al. ("the curve generated
    # by moving average" vs. "the original activity data").
    geom_line(data = curve, aes(x = tod, y = ma_y), color = "navy", linewidth = 0.9)

  if (nrow(other_peaks) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_point(data = other_peaks, aes(x = tod, y = y_cross),
                         color = "grey40", size = 1.5, shape = 1)
  }
  if (nrow(sel_points) > 0) {
    p <- p +
      geom_point(data = sel_points, aes(x = tod, y = y), color = "red", size = 3) +
      geom_text(data = sel_points, aes(x = tod, y = y, label = label), color = "red",
                vjust = -1, fontface = "bold", size = 4)
  }

  p +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 24), breaks = seq(0, 24, 4)) +
    labs(title = channel_label,
         subtitle = sprintf("has_M_peak = %s   has_E_peak = %s   (grey bars = raw activity, navy = moving-avg curve [intersected against raw], dotted grey = loess reference)",
                             !is.na(M_sel$tod), !is.na(E_sel$tod)),
         x = "Time of day (h)", y = "Activity") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey30"))
}

# ---- Generate a multi-page PDF, one page per channel, for one file.
# `channels = NULL` (default) reviews every channel, matching Vaze et
# al.'s practice of checking every individual's actogram, not just
# algorithmically-flagged ones. Pass a vector (e.g. from your
# needs_review output) to review only specific channels instead. ----
generate_review_pdf <- function(file_path, exclude_ch, LON, LOFF, species, photoperiod,
                                 output_pdf, channels = NULL) {
  profiles <- build_all_channel_profiles(file_path, exclude_ch)
  ch_list <- if (is.null(channels)) sort(unique(profiles$channel)) else sort(unique(channels))

  pdf(output_pdf, width = 8, height = 5)
  for (ch in ch_list) {
    sub <- profiles %>% filter(channel == ch)
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
    p <- plot_channel_diagnostic(
      sub$tod, sub$activity_mean, LON, LOFF, half_window_h,
      channel_label = sprintf("%s %s -- channel %d", species, photoperiod, ch)
    )
    print(p)
  }
  dev.off()

  message("Saved ", length(ch_list), " diagnostic pages to ", output_pdf)
}

# ============================================================
# RUN -- one PDF per species x photoperiod group, all channels.
# Swap in `channels = needs_review %>% filter(...) %>% pull(channel)`
# per group if you'd rather triage the flagged ones first.
# ============================================================
generate_review_pdf(pip_SD_file,  pip_SD_exclude_ch,  SD_LON, SD_LOFF, "Cxpip",  "SD", "review_Cxpip_SD.pdf")
generate_review_pdf(quin_SD_file, quin_SD_exclude_ch, SD_LON, SD_LOFF, "Cxquin", "SD", "review_Cxquin_SD.pdf")
generate_review_pdf(pip_LD_file,  pip_LD_exclude_ch,  LD_LON, LD_LOFF, "Cxpip",  "LD", "review_Cxpip_LD.pdf")
generate_review_pdf(quin_LD_file, quin_LD_exclude_ch, LD_LON, LD_LOFF, "Cxquin", "LD", "review_Cxquin_LD.pdf")
```
